notes: RESOLVED 2026-07-31, and the resolution is structural. The market was right and our observation feed was wrong BY CONSTRUCTION during the trading window. Two independent confirmations: (a) the METAR 6-hour max group covering the afternoon (18Z-00Z) is not transmitted until the 23:51Z report = 7:51 PM EDT, hours after we trade; the in-window group (13:51 EDT) only covers through 2 PM, and every hourly :51 snapshot after it read 78 while the continuous trace hit 80.06F at ~4:23 PM. (b) The NWS issues a PRELIMINARY CLI at ~20:35Z = ~4:35 PM EDT, and the 2026-07-29 20:32Z product already read MAXIMUM 80 at 227 PM - the settlement source itself published the answer inside the trading window, and we never looked at it.
lesson: TWO RULES. (1) Between ~2 PM and ~7:50 PM local our observed max is a LOWER BOUND that is biased LOW - the settlement-grade 6-hour group covering the afternoon has not been transmitted yet, so hourly snapshots can miss a between-obs spike of ~1F precisely during the hours we trade. A high-volume market pricing ONE BUCKET ABOVE our observed max is therefore evidence we are behind, not a mispricing to fade. (2) The fix is the ~4:35 PM EDT PRELIMINARY CLI: it is the settlement product, it is in-window, and it beats any METAR reconstruction. Caveat - it is a max-so-far, not a final: on Jul 30 the 4:36 PM prelim said 73 and the day finished 74 at 5:53 PM.

NEW LIMITATION FOUND: the 13:51 group covers only 8am-2pm, and the day's actual peak came at 2:28 PM -- 28 minutes AFTER that window closed. Our banked max therefore read 82.04 (->82) from 1:51pm onward while the truth was 82.94 (->83), and we stayed a degree low for six hours until the 19:51 group transmitted. The preliminary CLI at ~4:35pm revealed the true 83 first. Bucket outcome was unaffected (82 and 83 both sit in 82-83) but it would have mattered on a boundary day.
lesson: The 1:51 six-hour group is decisive but INCOMPLETE: it sees through 2 PM only, and NYC peaks routinely fall after that (2:28 PM today, 5:53 PM on Jul 30). Between 2 PM and 7:51 PM the only continuous-source reading available is the ~4:35 PM preliminary CLI -- which today was the first source to show the real max. Rule: after 2 PM, treat the 13:51 group as a LOWER BOUND on the day, not the day's max, and wait for the preliminary CLI before quoting a banked figure. Separately, the wet-day playbook held: the market moved 44c -> 99c on 82-83 through the day and every apparent opportunity was priced before it could be acted on.
